A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from DHMP to EvoMesh. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results on five datasets, including prediction errors, ablations, generalization tests, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds baseline comparisons, alternative-module experiments, and hierarchy-depth analyses.

M1.justification: The default architecture, loss, and hierarchical simulation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds implemented GATConv and cross-attention alternatives to AMP, constituting limited module adaptations. The expanded DiffSELECT and FeatureMixing descriptions clarify existing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CylinderFlow, Airfoil, Flag, DeformingPlate, and FoldingPaper, including changing meshes, unseen resolutions, and shifted input velocities. FlyingFlag is a renamed presentation of Flag; new ablations retain existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Eagle joins the standard and physical-variation comparisons. Resolution tests add MGN, Lino et al., and HCMT; physical-variation tests also add those comparators. Conversely, Table 13 drops MGN's efficiency comparison, and Figure 2 replaces its qualitative predictions with Lino et al.

E3.justification: Table 4 replaces full-rollout OOD-resolution evaluation with 50-step rollouts. New experiments vary hierarchy depth and AMP implementation and measure edge-enhancement time and memory. HCMT's description changes from 15 blocks to one message-passing step per level, without establishing reruns. The efficiency section also removes the stated less-than-1% convergence criterion.

E4.justification: v2 adds uniform-sampling ablation, GATConv/cross-attention comparisons, hierarchy-depth sensitivity, and computational analysis of edge enhancement. The original dynamic-hierarchy ablation is retained as M4, previously M3. The challenging-node analysis moves to Appendix C.5 rather than being removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three training seeds and three independent tests of a trained model. Added baseline rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline, ablation, depth, and resource results are added. In Table 2, MGN's Cylinder one-step error changes from 0.4046 to 0.3046 and Flag rollout error from 124.5 to 115.3, in the displayed units; the proposed model's scores remain unchanged. OOD rollout results are replaced under a different horizon. Eagle's Airfoil/Flag means conflict between v2 Tables 2 and 12.

T1.justification: No substantive theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added. The expanded Gumbel-Softmax and FeatureMixing equations explicate existing operations, and the cross-attention equation specifies an experimental variant.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the explicit 22.7% average improvement claim, while the introduction now reports approximately 20%. The central contributions—adaptive hierarchies, anisotropic propagation, and improved simulation accuracy—retain their original meaning.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies resolution generalization by acknowledging MGN's lower Flag and Plate errors. It adds possible overfitting and attention-redundancy explanations for new analyses. Its claim of consistent superiority over GAT overstates Table 9, where GAT slightly improves Flag one-step error. Existing interpretability and resolution limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with an availability statement and repository address. It newly documents the 1M-step budget, 500K-step learning-rate decay period, batch size, additional baseline configurations, FoldingPaper inputs/noise, and sampling details. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing that retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial positioning against differentiable pooling methods, including DiffPool, TopKPool, SAGPool, and ASAPooling, and expands attention and hierarchical-simulation coverage. The earlier absolute-position contrast with attention is replaced by discussion of weight application and reuse, materially refining the method's relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title and method are renamed, the abstract and introduction are extensively revised, and contributions receive an explicit list. Method explanations and related work are reorganized. Separate results appendices are consolidated into Appendix C, with baseline details moved to Appendix D.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Tables expand and are restructured, the ablation plot is redrawn, and new attention and depth displays appear. Seed-result tables and rollout-error figures are merged, while the challenging-node figure moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons and new sampling, attention, and depth controls strengthen the empirical assessment, while implementation and code-access information improve reproducibility. These gains are moderated by replacing full-rollout OOD results with shorter rollouts, removing MGN efficiency results, conflicting Eagle entries in Tables 2 and 12, and overstated GAT-comparison prose. The net improvement is useful but limited.
